adds.name: Lake Pueblo State Park (Juniper Breaks)
adds.waterfront_evidence: Esri imagery 2025-06-29 with all 84 cpwshop site GIS points plotted: the loops sit on the juniper bench above the north shore of Pueblo Reservoir; the nearest pads (181-183 above a narrow cove, 174-176 above the main lake) are ~35-45 m from the June 2025 waterline across a dirt track, scattered junipers and a rocky shore band, the rest 100+ m back; open ground keeps the water in view (lakeview, not lakefront).
adds.inclusion_evidence: cpwshop.com (parkID 50036) sells 84 Juniper Breaks sites (83 Basic + 1 Basic-ADA), all Drive-In RV/trailer sites with maximum vehicle lengths 30-65 ft (one unlisted); CPW 2024 brochure names 'Juniper Breaks Campground' as a campground of its own -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft motorhome fits.
adds.note: North-shore campground of Lake Pueblo State Park, reached by its own road (Juniper Road) about 1.5 km east of the Northern Plains loops; the loops string along a juniper bench above Pueblo Reservoir's north shore and coves. --Claude

sites.note: 84 basic sites (100-183, 157HD ADA), no electricity; cpwshop lists vehicles to 30-65 ft (40 or 45 ft at most), one site with no length.

facilities.note: Central water hydrants and vault toilets; the dump stations are in the Northern Plains and Arkansas Point campgrounds.

season.note: CPW: camping is available year-round and only the Northern Plains campgrounds close for winter; limited sites and amenities in winter.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com, 1-800-244-5613, or at the park office, up to six months ahead. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people, two motorized vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

fees.note: Every Juniper Breaks site is basic: $28 a night, Saturday the same. Plus tax, CPW's per-stay reservation fee, and a vehicle pass ($4 a day to $80 a year per CPW's park page) or an annual Colorado state parks pass.

adds.name: Navajo State Park (Tiffany)
adds.waterfront_evidence: Esri imagery 2022-10-29 + CPW Tiffany campground map: the north loop and the south (cabin) loop sit on a bench above Navajo Reservoir; the nearest RV pads are ~100 m from the Oct 2022 waterline across a juniper-dotted scarp and the bare drawdown band (pads ~8 m above full pool by DEM), and the water is lower now (CPW: historic low) -> view, not lakefront.
adds.inclusion_evidence: cpwshop.com (parkID 50033) sells 25 Tiffany RV sites (24 Basic 101-118/125-130 + Full Hookup site 100) with maximum vehicle lengths 20-55 ft, 21 of them 25 ft or more (11 pull-throughs to 55 ft); CPW camping page: 'Tiffany has basic RV sites ... as well as a restroom and shower house' -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft motorhome fits.
adds.note: Navajo State Park's basic-site campground on its own spur road just southwest of Carracas: a north loop of RV sites and a south loop with the park's three cabins and walk-in tent sites, on a bench above Navajo Reservoir. --Claude

sites.note: 25 RV sites: 24 basic plus full-hookup site 100 (30 ft). cpwshop vehicle lengths: ten at 55 ft (mostly pull-throughs), two 45, one 35, two 30, six 25, four 20 (102, 114, 127, 129, too short for 23 ft). Six walk-in tent sites (119-124) and three cabins not counted.

hookups.note: Only site 100 has hookups; its cpwshop page lists 'Full Hookup: 50' but also 'Electricity Hookup: 15'. The 24 basic sites have none.

facilities.note: Restroom and shower house (push-button showers); camper services and restroom buildings close September 16 to April 14, when the park has vault toilets only. The dump station is in Carracas next door.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead; reservations cannot be made at the park. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people, two motorized vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

fees.note: Basic sites $28 a night in June, Saturday the same; full-hookup site 100 $41 (CPW's park page gives $14-$41 for a campsite). Plus tax, CPW's per-stay reservation fee, and a daily vehicle pass ($10-$15) or an annual Colorado state parks pass.

adds.name: Navajo State Park (Windsurf Beach)
adds.waterfront_evidence: Esri imagery 2022-10-29 + CPW Windsurf Beach map + OSM loop way 1148906002: the loop sits on the west edge of the drained reservoir bed; open water is gone, the nearest water is the Piedra/San Juan river channel ~300 m NE across dry lakebed, and every cpwshop site page now says 'Due to historic low water levels, the Arboles Point Campground and Windsurf Beach Campground are not on the water or near the reservoir at this time' -> not waterfront at current water (cpwshop's 'Lakefront' tag is the full-pool condition).
adds.inclusion_evidence: cpwshop.com (parkID 50033) sells 20 Windsurf Beach Primitive Drive-In RV sites (401-420), 12 of them 25 ft or more and seven pull-throughs of 35-80 ft. CPW calls them 'smaller, primitive campsites better for tents or small RVs', but CPW's own per-site lengths show a 23-ft rig fits 12 sites (curation rule: a stated length that fits outranks the 'small RVs' wording) -> keep.
adds.note: Primitive campground off County Road 982 north of the main park, on the west shore of the reservoir's Piedra arm. With the reservoir at historic low water, CPW says the campground is no longer on or near the water. CPW calls the sites better for tents or small RVs. --Claude

sites.note: 20 primitive drive-in sites (401-420), gravel with a slight grade (406 and 414 paved). cpwshop vehicle lengths: 80, 65 x2, 50 x3, 35 and 30 (the pull-throughs and 408), 25 x4 (401-403, 405), 20 x8 (404, 406, 410-415, too short for 23 ft).

facilities.note: Pit toilets only, no water; fill tanks at the park's main entrance.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead; reservations cannot be made at the park. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people, two motorized vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

fees.note: Primitive sites $14 a night in June, Saturday the same. Plus tax, CPW's per-stay reservation fee, and a daily vehicle pass ($10-$15) or an annual Colorado state parks pass.

adds.name: Navajo State Park (Arboles Point)
adds.waterfront_evidence: Esri imagery 2022-10-29 + CPW Arboles Point map + OSM ways 490728685/490728687: the four sites sit on a juniper point 6-9 m (DEM) above the drained reservoir bed at the San Juan/Piedra confluence; the nearest water is the river channel ~200 m west of sites 1-3 across open dry lakebed (the reservoir pool ~850 m east), and cpwshop: 'Due to historic low water levels, the Arboles Point Campground ... not on the water or near the reservoir at this time'; CPW: 'stunning views of the San Juan River' -> riverview.
adds.inclusion_evidence: cpwshop.com (parkID 50033) sells 4 Arboles Point Primitive Drive-In double RV sites (501-504) with maximum vehicle lengths 45-60 ft (two pull-throughs); CPW camping page: 'Arboles Point Campground ... only 4 double sites'; no 4WD or high-clearance wording on CPW's pages -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft motorhome fits.
adds.note: Four double sites on a point off County Road 500 (Trujillo Road), east of Arboles, where the Piedra River arm meets the San Juan arm. With the reservoir at historic low water, CPW says the campground is no longer on or near the water. Site 501's driveway grade is severe. Unplowed in winter. --Claude

sites.note: 4 primitive drive-in double sites (12 people, 4 vehicles, 2 camping units each): 501 45-ft pull-through (gravel, severe grade), 502 55-ft back-in (moderate grade), 503 50-ft pull-through (paved), 504 60-ft back-in.

facilities.note: Pit toilets only, no water; fill tanks at the park's main entrance.

booking.note: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead; reservations cannot be made at the park. 14 days within a 28-day period; each double site holds 12 people, four vehicles and two camping units. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.

fees.note: Double primitive sites $20 a night in June, Saturday the same. Plus tax, CPW's per-stay reservation fee, and a daily vehicle pass ($10-$15) or an annual Colorado state parks pass.
